title: Long AMZN — AWS Cloud AI Capex Read-Through
entry: Buy the current consolidation zone at $260-$268. Scale: 60% at current; add 40% on either a pullback to $255 or a confirmed break above $272 on volume.
stop_loss: $248 daily close (~6.4% below entry midpoint) — implies AWS growth deceleration or consumer demand cracking
targets: $295 — new all-time high on AWS guide raise, +11.3%
catalyst: NVDA's $91B Q2 guide is the strongest leading indicator for AWS revenue in 4-8 weeks. AWS processed 36% YoY revenue growth in Q1 2026 — accelerating sequentially. Every dollar of hyperscaler AI capex that NVDA's supply chain is absorbing flows directly to AWS infrastructure capacity. Amazon disclosed $6B in new data center commitments in the most recent earnings period; the $91B NVDA Q2 guide implies these commitments will be front-loaded.
thesis:
AWS is the largest public cloud by revenue and processes the majority of enterprise AI inference and training workloads. NVDA's $91B Q2 guide creates a direct read-through: if hyperscalers are collectively committing $91B to NVDA GPU supply in a single quarter, the cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) must be simultaneously expanding capacity to host those GPUs. AWS's competitive advantage is scale and ecosystem depth — the Bedrock AI platform, SageMaker infrastructure, and the broader enterprise software stack mean AWS captures both the raw compute revenue and the application-layer services revenue as AI adoption expands.

The tactical advantage of AMZN over NVDA right now is the absence of near-term binary risk. NVDA is in the 'beats and drops' pattern post-earnings, creating a consolidation period with unclear direction in the next 5-10 trading sessions. AMZN has no earnings until late July — the 4-8 week window is exactly the catalyst-free runway needed for the AI capex read-through to be reflected in the stock price ahead of the earnings catalyst. AMZN's 52-week range ($196-$278.56) means the $265 entry is below the 52-week high, leaving room for a new ATH breakout without requiring an extreme move.

The position is sized at 4% (medium, not high) because AMZN is not a clean single-factor AI play. The retail and advertising segments (~60% of revenue) face independent headwinds: 30Y at 5.12% pressures consumer confidence and mortgage-sensitive spending; PCE on May 27 will confirm whether inflation is sticky enough to affect discretionary retail. The thesis requires AWS to drive margin expansion fast enough to offset any retail softness — which is the consensus analyst view (62 buy recommendations, 0 sells) but not guaranteed.

The counter-party to this trade is the institutional manager selling AMZN in the next 22 days to fund a SpaceX IPO allocation. SPCX's $75B raise will require portfolio rebalancing across growth-oriented funds, and AMZN — as a $2.79T market cap member of every major benchmark — will receive some of those sell orders. This is a headwind in the 0-3 week window; the 4-8 week thesis absorbs the IPO-selling and positions for the July earnings catalyst.
bull_case: AWS Q2 revenue growth accelerates to 40%+ YoY (vs 36% in Q1); Amazon Bedrock enterprise adoption surges (Fortune 500 companies lock in multi-year AI contracts); AMZN raises FY26 operating income guide at July earnings. Stock breaks above $278 52-week high, trades to new ATH at $295-$315 range. Tail: SpaceX IPO drives general 'tech is back' sentiment post-June 12 debut; AMZN benefits from the rising tide.
bear_case: Consumer spending cracks on PCE hot print (May 27) + 30Y persistence; Amazon retail margins compress in Q2; AWS growth stalls at 28-30% as enterprise AI adoption is slower to monetize than NVDA's supply data suggests. Stock pulls toward $248-$252 stop zone. Tail: SpaceX IPO selling pressure is concentrated in megacap tech in the June 4-12 window; AMZN experiences unusual selling before the thesis can play out.
invalidation: Daily close below $248, OR AWS Q2 growth guide below 28% YoY (would require an early update or an analyst estimate revision that implies this)
